archetype.name: Point Guard (with a gunslinger's deep shot)
archetype.definition: A quick-game distributor who throws three of every four passes at or behind 9 air yards, spreads the ball across five regular targets, and still takes enough deep shots to swing a game either way.

report.headline: Same efficient Mahomes as recent years, with red-zone touchdowns flattering the line
report.take:
The 4-0 record and a top-eight touchdown count read like a return to his peak, but the per-play numbers tell a calmer story. His 0.192 EPA per dropback ranks 13th, which is nearly where he finished in 2023 through 2025 (14th, 15th, 13th). Those were good seasons, well short of the 2018-2022 run when he sat in the top six every year. This is a quick, horizontal offense now: 95 of his 128 attempts landed at or behind 9 air yards, his intended air yards sit at 7.12, and he throws about 1.4 yards short of the sticks on average. Andy Reid has built a point-guard offense around him, and it has worked. Short throws are producing 0.302 EPA with six touchdowns.

What lifts the line from good to glossy is the red zone. Nine touchdowns on 26 red-zone attempts with a +20 CPOE is a finishing rate no quarterback holds, and it is why his ANY/A ranks 6th while his EPA ranks 13th. The accuracy underneath is ordinary: CPOE ranks 28th, the tracking-based CPOE is negative, and 14.1% of his throws are charted as bad, 26th of 36. The middle of the field has been a problem: -0.091 EPA, a -8 CPOE and both of his interceptions. His success is coming from the boundaries, where throws to the left and right are each producing well over 0.3 EPA.

Two things have genuinely improved. After a 2025 in which 28.8% of his pressures became sacks (28th), that rate is down to 19.4% (10th), closer to his early-career profile. He also looks sharp in tight spots, with 0.435 EPA on 22 fourth-quarter plays in close games. The legs have mostly disappeared, though. Last year he ran for 422 yards, 5th at the position. This year it is 41 yards on 12 carries with negative rushing EPA, and only 8 scrambles. Those scrambles have been efficient, so this looks like a choice or a scheme change rather than a lost skill, but it removes a fantasy cushion.

The receiver room is about to change. Tyquan Thornton was his most efficient target by a wide margin (1.269 EPA on 15 targets) and is now on IR. Rashee Rice's hamstring is described as minor, with the bye giving him time. Travis Kelce at 0.744 EPA per target is the engine. Xavier Worthy has drawn as many targets as Kelce while producing negative EPA, and he likely absorbs more of Thornton's role. That is a downgrade in vertical efficiency unless Rice is back at full speed.

strengths.title: Quick game that produces explosive EPA
strengths.body: His short passing (0-9 air yards) is producing 0.302 EPA with six touchdowns and no interceptions. That pairs an offense built on timing with a quarterback who rarely wastes those snaps. It is a schematic identity he has leaned into for three years running (aDOT 6.3-7.9 since 2023), so it should hold, even if the touchdown count on those throws cools.

strengths.title: Sacks avoided under pressure again
strengths.body: Only 19.4% of his pressures have turned into sacks, 10th in the league. That is a sharp recovery from 2025's 28.8%, which ranked 28th, and much closer to his 2018-2023 range. With a 2.7-second time to throw and a quick-game structure, this improvement looks real rather than lucky. It matters this week against a defense that gets home often.

strengths.title: Kelce connection carrying the passing game
strengths.body: Kelce's 0.744 EPA per target on 22 targets makes him the most reliable route in the offense. He gives Mahomes a dependable answer on third down and in the red zone. That reliance is sustainable as long as Kelce stays healthy, and it grows in importance with Thornton gone.

concerns.title: Red-zone touchdown rate will regress
concerns.body: All nine of his passing touchdowns have come on 26 red-zone attempts, with a +20 CPOE inside the 20 against a 0.8 CPOE overall. That gap is a small-sample hot streak, not a skill change. His touchdown pace should drift toward the low 20s over a full season, as it did in 2024 and 2025.

concerns.title: Middle-of-field accuracy and bad throws
concerns.body: Throws to the middle have produced negative EPA with a -8 CPOE and both interceptions. His bad-throw rate ranks 26th of 36, and Week 4 at Las Vegas hit 25.9% when he was pressured on a third of dropbacks. This continues a two-year slide in accuracy metrics: his CPOE ranked 33rd in 2025, so it looks more like the current version of him than a blip.

concerns.title: Losing his best vertical target
concerns.body: Thornton led the room at 1.269 EPA per target and is on IR into January. Worthy, who has seen 22 targets at -0.152 EPA, is the obvious beneficiary of the extra volume. Deep throws are already only 38.9% complete with two picks. Unless Rice returns healthy, the explosive ceiling of this passing game shrinks.

trend.note: His passing EPA by week went -2.3, +13.4, +12.9 and +1.7. Two sharp games against bottom-five defenses (IND, MIA) are bookended by shaky outings against Denver and Las Vegas, where his CPOE was -11.9 and -7.3.

nextGame.headline: Rested Chiefs host a broken Chargers offense; Mahomes may not need volume
nextGame.body:
The Chargers' defense is the real thing in most respects. It ranks 6th in EPA and 8th against the pass, and it is 4th in hit rate, so his improved sack avoidance gets tested. It has also held quarterbacks to the 5th-fewest passing yards a game. The soft spot is deep: the Chargers allow 0.712 EPA on deep throws (22nd) and rank 22nd in explosive pass rate. That fits a Mahomes who still takes his shots, though his deep efficiency has been all-or-nothing. The bigger factor may be game script. The Chargers' offense ranks last in EPA, last in passing EPA and last in pass rate over expected, which points to a low-possession, field-position game. A Chiefs offense ranked 2nd in rushing EPA could lean on the run with a lead.

Availability tilts toward Kansas City. The Chargers are without both starting tackles (Slater on IR, Alt out) and two guards (Awosika out, Penning on IR). Their receiver group is gutted, with Johnston out, Harris doubtful and McConkey questionable. Derwin James, a 94%-snap safety, is out along with corners Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, which thins the secondary Mahomes faces. On his side, Rice is listed questionable but was expected back after the bye. Thornton's absence removes his most efficient target, and tackle Josh Simmons, questionable, has not played a snap this season. The early forecast shows 16 mph wind with 27 mph gusts. It is five days out, but if it holds it would cap the deep game and lean the total down.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers pass rush vs quick game
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers are 4th in hit rate and 10th in sack rate. His answer has been getting the ball out, at 2.7 seconds with a 19.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But when Las Vegas pressured him on 33% of dropbacks, his bad-throw rate jumped to 25.9%.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a thinned secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers bleed EPA on deep throws, and Derwin James plus two corners are out. That is where Mahomes can hit for a big play, though without Thornton and possibly in gusting wind, the volume of those shots is uncertain.

keyMatchups.title: Game script favors the Chiefs' run game
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers' offense is last in passing EPA and missing both tackles, so Kansas City should play from ahead. With the league's 2nd-best rushing EPA, the Chiefs have reason to shorten the game, which caps Mahomes's attempts.

nextGame.watch: Whether Rice is active and gets a full workload, and whether Worthy finally turns his volume into positive plays with Thornton gone.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the 2023-2025 version of Mahomes: an efficient, quick-game operator around the 12th-15th range in EPA per dropback, winning with timing, Kelce and a strong run game rather than volume or deep efficiency. The sack-avoidance rebound looks real given the structure of the offense. The red-zone touchdown rate and the +20 red-zone CPOE will not last, so his touchdown pace should slow from 2.25 a game toward the 1.6-1.9 range. Passing yardage should hold near the mid-200s against average defenses.

The swing piece is the receiving corps. A healthy Rice alongside Kelce keeps the efficiency up. A Worthy-heavy target tree without Thornton likely drags the deep game and his bad-throw-prone middle reads further down. His rushing, nearly absent so far, is the one area with upside if Reid lets him run like he did in 2025.

bets.reason: The Chargers allow the 5th-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks, and the game script projects a Chiefs lead behind a top-two rushing offense. His most efficient target is on IR, and an early forecast of 27 mph gusts would only push this further under.

The Chargers' offense is last in EPA and passing EPA, runs more than any team in neutral situations, and is missing both tackles, two guards and most of its receivers. A top-10 defense on the other side and possible wind make a high-scoring game unlikely.

The Chiefs come off a bye at home against an opponent whose offense ranks 32nd and has lost most of its line and receivers. The number is big for a division game, and the Chiefs' pass rush ranks 31st in sack rate, which keeps it from being a stronger play.

confidence.note: Four games, two against bottom-five defenses, and a receiver room in flux; the career baseline is stable.
